newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ponders stance on climate change goals.
newsitem.headline: EU ponders stance on climate change goals.

text.p: European Union environment ministers struggled on Monday to set targets for post-2000 cuts in the bloc's emissions of greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide with agreement stuck on how far and how fast to go.

Ministers abandoned efforts to reach agreement after two hours of talks early on Monday, returning later to consider a text drawn up by EU president Ireland committing the bloc's 15 countries to cuts of between five and 10 percent of greenhouse gases by the year 2005 based on 1990 levels.
"There's a body of countries...who believe that we have got to commit ourselves to significant targets after the year 2000," British Environment Minister John Gummer told reporters.
The text also foresees 10-20 percent cuts by 2010.

The term greenhouse gases, which includes methane and the chlorofluorocarbon-type substances used as refrigerants and aerosol propellants, refers to human-generated gases which trap solar energy in the atmosphere in a global-warming "greenhouse effect".

One EU official said countries were divided between those wanting more than proposed, such as Germany, Austria and Denmark, those backing the the text, namely Britain, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg and Finland, and the others.
France and Sweden wanted EU offers of cuts to be based on tonnes per capita rather than on absolute figures while Spain, Portugal and Greece wanted less-severe cuts.

The EU position, once fixed, will bear on United Nations negotiators' efforts at meetings in Geneva this week and in the coming months during preparations for a binding protocol on cuts slated for agreement in 1997.
German representative Angela Merkel said that if ministers failed to agree sufficently ambitious cuts she would prefer to leave a deal on the EU's position until later.
